action: Cut the homepage from seven bands to three at the owner's request
reason: The owner reviewed the full page and found it too long. Their decision, made with the finished version in front of them.
kept: [lookdog_hero] - kept because removing it leaves the page with no H1 and no statement of what the site is
[lookdog_category_grid] - Browse by what it is, six cards, with the one-line link to the problem pages
removed_from_the_page: [lookdog_drawbacks] - the band that quoted real Cons lines from real product pages
[lookdog_method] - How things get on this site
[lookdog_featured_guide] - the newest guide with its pull quote
[lookdog_guides_index] - the list of all seven guides
no_code_deleted: All four shortcodes still ship and still work. Each gates its own CSS on the shortcode being present, so an unused one prints nothing at all. Restoring any of them is one line in post_content.

consequences.issue: The guides have no homepage entry point
consequences.checked: All 7 remain linked from /blog/ (HTTP 200), the Blog nav item is on every page, and the 'Before you buy' block on all 167 product pages still points at them. The link graph is intact; the path from the front door is longer.

consequences.issue: Trust content is down to the hero's one line
consequences.note: The method band carried the 80% feedback floor, the category count and the both-sides promise at length. The hero trust strip still carries the short version, with live numbers.

band_grounds: The category band was switched from tint to white. With the drawbacks band gone it would otherwise have sat on the same ground as the rail directly above it, and the two sections would have run together.

list: #categories anchor kept for the hero button
verification.page_weight: body markup 68,793 bytes, down from 74,830 before the audit work began
verification.headings: H1 Dog gear, with the drawbacks written down / H2 What people actually buy / H2 Browse by what it is / six H3 category names / H2 Shop / H2 The small print
